title: NoiseCLR: A Contrastive Learning Approach for Unsupervised Discovery of Interpretable Directions in Diffusion Models
role: The closest working contrastive objective on the brief's d_t quantity (conditional minus null noise prediction), with positives paired across images
reads: Feature divergence eps_theta(x_t, d_k) - eps_theta(x_t, null) for a learned direction d_k fed as the condition, at forward-noised real images, all timesteps
trains: Only K learned directions (100 for faces and art, 50 for cats and cars) on about 100 unlabeled images per domain, frozen SD 1.5, contrastive loss with cosine similarity, tau 0.5, AdamW lr 1e-3, batch 6, about 7 h on one L40
combines: Cosine similarity of divergences: same direction on different images attract, different directions on the same noisy image repel; edits add lambda_e (eps(x_t, d_e) - eps(x_t, null)) to the CFG prediction
adding: Assumes the conditional-minus-null difference carries the condition's meaning and that summed directions do not interfere because they are disentangled; no proof, qualitative evidence, and a Child edit moves Indian by -37.7 CLIP points
noise_and_seed: not addressed (one fixed seed 0; positives across images push for noise-invariant divergences but no cosine reported)
timesteps: not measured quantitatively; edits applied from t = 0.5T, coarse edits in [0.9T, 0.8T]; early steps change more (qualitative, 50-step ablation)
unseen: no + no held-out concepts; face directions transfer to paintings and stack within and across domains, qualitatively only
headline: User-rated disentanglement 3.05 on a 1-to-5 scale vs 2.73 for Cycle-Diffusion (50 MTurk raters), edit quality 2.65 vs 2.19 Composable Diffusion, Stable Diffusion 1.5
suggests: (inferred) Pair positives as the same caption across different canvases and seeds, as NoiseCLR pairs the same direction across images, and measure cross-seed cosine of d_t before training

quotes.text: we first define the feature divergences ∆ϵnk caused by an arbitrary direction dk on an arbitrary data sample xn as follows
∆ϵnk = ϵθ (xnt , dk ) − ϵθ (xnt , ϕ)
while learning directions by considering all timesteps of the diffusion model
In our default setting, we train NoiseCLR with N = 100, K = 100 and τ = 0.5
To optimize the directions, we use a learning rate of 10−3 and batch size of 6 for AdamW optimizer
training our method on a single domain requires approximately 7 hours to learn 100 directions in face domain
we want for edits carried out by the same direction to be attracted towards each other, while edits conducted by different directions to repel one another
To express the semantic similarity between a pair of target feature differences, we use cosine similarity
Leveraging the observation that the difference ϵθ (xt , c) − ϵθ (xt , ϕ) encodes semantic information encoded by the condition c
Since we formulate editing for an arbitrary direction as a summation of predicted noises for a given timestep t, we are able to perform multiple edits
applying the edit of ”Child” significantly changes the race-based edits
To ensure the reproducibility of our experiments, we conduct all experiments with a fixed random seed of 0
As a rule of thumb, we apply the discovered edits starting from t = 0.5T
applying edits at earlier denoising steps result in more significant changes in the input image
face edits generalize well to artistic paintings
NoiseCLR can discover directions not explicitly represented in the input dataset but still compatible with the domain of the training images
an user study conducted on 50 participants using Amazon Mturk platform
The scoring is performed within the scale of 1-to-5
We used Stable Diffusion-v1.5 for all of our experiments
